# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🫳 ✍ ✋ 👍 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 👉]

**Thinking.** Let me map who can reach whom. Mute can hear me but can only answer by gesture, which I can see. Blind can speak, but I cannot hear — Blind's only line to me is gesture, while Blind's speech reaches Mute. Crucially, **Mute and Blind have no channel between them at all**: Mute can't speak, Blind can't see gestures. So I am the only bridge — whatever Mute's manual says must come to me by gesture, and I relay it to Blind by speech.

Mute's opening gesture [👉 🫳 ✍ ✋ 👍 👌] is probably a handshake or an undecodable attempt at manual instructions — we have no shared code yet, and ✍ alone hints "manual". Blind's [👋 🫴 👉] reads like "hello, I'm here, direct me." I can't decode either reliably, so my priority is to establish a code and report the bomb.

What I see: display 0, light off, plate engraved "?", wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Blind can't use colours, so I'll anchor the wire order to something tactile — the display is a physical part Blind can feel. I'll tell Mute the code and the state so the manual can be checked, and tell Blind the state, the anchoring, and the relay protocol. Nobody should cut anything yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Bomb report: display reads 0, light is off, plate is engraved with a question mark, three wires in order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. You and Blind cannot reach each other directly, so relay everything through me: you gesture, I speak to them. Please adopt this gesture code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, OK sign understood, writing hand means 'manual instruction follows', then number gestures for wires: one is index finger, two is victory fingers, three is the three-finger sign. Fist means cut the wire, raised open hand means stop or don't cut. I could not decode your last message, so resend any manual instruction using this code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is off, plate is engraved with a question mark, and there are three wires. Feel for them: wire 1 is the one nearest the display, then wire 2, then wire 3; nearest is red, middle blue, last green, though you cannot see colour. Protocol: Mute has the manual but cannot speak, and you two have no channel between you. So speak your findings aloud, Mute hears them, Mute gestures them to me, and I relay instructions to you by speech. I cannot hear you, so gesture me anything meant for me alone: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Feel the bomb now and confirm the display, light, plate and three wires, and describe by voice anything you feel that I might not see: buttons, batteries, markings. Do not cut anything until an instruction from me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✍ ✊ 🤟 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** Decoding Mute against our agreed code: 👌 understood, ✍ manual instruction follows, ✊ fist = cut the wire, 🤟 = the three-finger sign = wire 3, 👍 = yes/confirmed. That reads as a complete, deliberate instruction: **cut wire 3**. Crucially, Mute formed it knowing the exact state I reported last round (display 0, light off, plate "?", three wires red/blue/green), so it already accounts for what we see. Blind's 👍 confirms they understood the protocol and are on board.

Before Blind cuts, I must anchor wire 3 in touch, not colour: wire 3 is the one farthest from the display, the last of three. And I'll guard against my view and Blind's hands disagreeing — if what Blind feels doesn't match my report, no cut. The board shows no timer, but I won't spend a whole round re-asking Mute for permission; the instruction was explicit and self-affirming. Instead I'll execute it conditionally and simultaneously ask Mute to flag any missed condition, plus request next steps for after the cut.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Decoded instruction from Mute, via gesture: cut wire 3. Anchor it by touch: the bomb has a display, then a plate, then a row of exactly three wires. Wire 1 is nearest the display, wire 3 is the farthest from the display, the last one in the row. Do this now: first feel and confirm you find the display, the engraved plate, and exactly three wires in a row. If all of that matches, cut wire 3, the one farthest from the display. If anything does not match — a missing part, a fourth wire, a button I did not report — do not cut. Instead gesture me thumbs down and speak aloud what you feel so Mute can hear it. After you cut, speak aloud everything that changes: any number on the display, whether a light comes on, any sound, so Mute hears it and can instruct us further.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I received your gesture as: understood, manual instruction, cut, wire 3, yes. I have relayed to Blind: confirm by touch that the layout matches my report, then cut the wire farthest from the display, which is wire 3. Confirm my reading of your code: gesture thumbs up if cut wire 3 is unconditional and I read you correctly. Gesture the stop hand if the instruction had conditions I must check first, and show me which. Also tell me what should happen after the cut: what change should I watch for on the display or the light, and what the manual says the next step will be. After the cut I will report you exactly what I see. If Blind's touch does not match my view, they will gesture me thumbs down and speak findings you will hear; encode those for me next round.")
```
